rationale: The Candidate summary closely matches the Reference in scope, translating vision findings into practical OT implications including O&M referral, environmental modification, eyewear guidance, and participation/transport planning. All clinical findings and management suggestions largely align with the SOURCE, but the falls-risk level is understated (Moderate vs High), and the optometrist's urgent GP/systemic work-up recommendation was omitted; a minor pronoun error was also present. These issues do not prevent clinical use but require correction to ensure appropriate prioritisation and communication.

The candidate captures the core diagnosis, diplopia-related mobility issues, and the basic recommendation to consider O&M and safer eyewear, so it is directionally useful. However, it underplays the risk level and misses several OT-relevant safety priorities from the reference, especially home safety, indoor access, and the urgency/functional specificity of mobility support. There is also some unsupported or imprecise phrasing, but the main concern is clinically important omission and risk underestimation.

The candidate summary accurately reflects the source clinical findings and the reference OT-focused recommendations, covering mobility risk, spectacle-use behaviour, functional impacts, and appropriate OT strategies. Only minor reference-level details (local advocacy for pavement repair, explicit distance orthophoria, and the specific note about initial increased fall risk with multifocals) were omitted, but there are no factual errors or unsafe recommendations.

The candidate captures the core case: correctable distance blur, inconsistent spectacle use when mobilising, and the need for consistent distance correction and follow-up. However, it adds several unsupported functional inferences and overemphasises binocular findings as mobility-relevant, while missing some practical OT strategies from the reference. Overall it is usable with edits, but not fully aligned due to the safety-relevant interpretation issue.

The candidate summary captures the same key vision findings, functional impacts, environmental considerations, falls risk rating, and OT/O&M referral priorities as the reference and is consistent with the source report. It avoids inventing unsupported clinical or social details and stays within appropriate OT scope, providing safe, practical assessment and intervention recommendations suitable for an OT handover.

The candidate captures the core issue of progressive glaucoma with peripheral/spatial awareness loss, reduced contrast sensitivity, near-miss history in dim hallways, and the main OT priorities of lighting, clutter reduction, and O&M referral. However, it adds multiple unsupported functional and environmental details and expands into OT-driving and assistive-device guidance beyond what the source establishes. The result is usable but not equivalent to the reference because of these extra inferences and somewhat over-extended recommendations.
